items.title: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
items.summary: Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique apart from the order of factors.
steps: Divide the number by the smallest prime that divides it.
Continue factoring each composite quotient until every factor is prime.
Arrange the prime factors in non-decreasing order.
Uniqueness follows from Euclid's lemma: if a prime divides a product, it divides at least one factor.
items.examTip: Use prime factorisation to find HCF and LCM; show the factor tree or division steps.

items.title: Prime factorisation method
items.summary: Express each composite integer as a product of primes; compare prime powers to obtain HCF and LCM.

Product of all prime factors with the greatest powers

items.title: Irrationality proof pattern
items.summary: To prove a square root of a non-square integer is irrational, assume a reduced fraction and derive a contradiction.
steps: Assume √p = a/b, where gcd(a,b)=1.
Square both sides: a² = p b².
Use prime divisibility to show p divides a, then p divides b.
This contradicts gcd(a,b)=1.

items.title: Relationship between zeroes and coefficients (quadratic)
items.summary: For p(x) = ax² + bx + c, with zeroes α and β: α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a.
steps: Factorise p(x) as a(x − α)(x − β).
Expand: a[x² − (α + β)x + αβ].
Compare coefficients with ax² + bx + c.
Equate x-coefficients and constant terms to obtain the relationships.
items.examTip: State the degree and leading coefficient before applying the relationships.

items.title: Consistency conditions
items.summary: For a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0, the ratios determine the number of solutions.
steps: Unique solution: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂; the lines intersect.
No solution: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂; the lines are parallel.
Infinitely many solutions: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂; the lines coincide.

items.title: Sum of first n terms
items.summary: Pair the first and last terms to derive the AP sum.
steps: Write Sₙ = a + (a+d) + … + l.
Reverse the order: Sₙ = l + (l−d) + … + a.
Add the two equations; each pair equals a + l.
Thus 2Sₙ = n(a+l), so Sₙ = n/2(a+l).

items.title: Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales)
items.summary: A line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio.
steps: In ΔABC, let D lie on AB and E on AC with DE ∥ BC.
Triangles ADE and BDE have equal altitude to AB, so their area ratio is AD:DB.
Similarly compare areas using the common altitude to AC.
Using the equal areas of triangles sharing base DE and parallel lines, obtain AD/DB = AE/EC.

items.summary: P = perpendicular, B = base, H = hypotenuse in a right triangle.

items.title: Fundamental identity
items.summary: Divide the Pythagorean relation P² + B² = H² by H².
steps: Start with P² + B² = H².
Divide every term by H².
Recognise P/H = sin θ and B/H = cos θ.
Therefore sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
items.examTip: Also derive 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

items.title: Tangents from an external point
items.summary: The lengths of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
steps: Let PA and PB be tangents from P, touching at A and B.
Join OA, OB and OP.
OA ⟂ PA and OB ⟂ PB (radius is perpendicular to tangent).
OA = OB (radii) and OP is common.
Right triangles OAP and OBP are congruent by RHS; hence PA = PB.

items.title: Equal tangents theorem
items.summary: Tangents drawn from the same external point to a circle have equal lengths.
steps: Let PA and PB touch the circle at A and B; join OA, OB and OP.
OA=OB (radii).
OA⊥PA and OB⊥PB.
OP is common; the right triangles are congruent by RHS.
Therefore PA=PB.

items.summary: An event and its complement are mutually exclusive and together cover the entire sample space.

items.title: Electric power and heating
items.formula: P = VI = I²R = V²/R · H = I²Rt

items.title: Equivalent resistance in series
items.summary: The same current flows through each resistor in a series circuit.
steps: Let the potential differences be V₁ and V₂ across R₁ and R₂.
Total potential difference V = V₁ + V₂.
By Ohm's law, IRₛ = IR₁ + IR₂.
Cancel I: Rₛ = R₁ + R₂. For more resistors, add all resistances.

items.title: Equivalent resistance in parallel
items.summary: The potential difference across each parallel branch is the same.
steps: Let branch currents be I₁ and I₂; total current I = I₁ + I₂.
By Ohm's law, I = V/Rₚ, I₁ = V/R₁ and I₂ = V/R₂.
Substitute: V/Rₚ = V/R₁ + V/R₂.
Cancel V: 1/Rₚ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.

items.title: Joule's law of heating
items.summary: Electrical energy converted into heat in a resistor.
steps: Electrical work done W = VQ.
Since Q = It, W = VIt.
Using Ohm's law V = IR, obtain H = I²Rt.
